maya: Heads up — after the rollout I can reproduce cross-org project listings. A user from org-b can GET /v1/orgs/org-a/projects and receives a 200 with project metadata. Repro steps and logs below.

maya: Reproducer:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer user-token-from-org-b" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org-a/projects"
# => 200 OK, payload includes projects belonging to org-a
```

oliver: which deploy? commit/PR? :eyes:

maya: PR #3421 (eng-platform) merged routing change for namespace resolution. Rollout started 2026-03-20T12:05:00Z. Router logs show the incoming request had x-org: org-b but resolved to org-a namespace backend. Snippet:
```
router: req_id=0a1b2c src_ip=10.11.12.13 src_org=org-b path=/v1/orgs/org-a/projects target_namespace=org-a resolved_account=org-a route_version=v2
```

rachel: Can we stop the rollout? Do we have a canary toggle?

oliver: I flipped the feature flag for namespace-routing back to v1 (flag: routing.namespace_resolver_v2) — that should stop new traffic hitting the new code. Need to confirm if any cached mappings are sticky.

maya: Quick mitigation: blocked path via WAF for non-admins: `/v1/orgs/*/projects` from outside org header. It's a band-aid.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-045 (severity: P2) — channel: #eng-security, oncall: rachel

oliver: Root cause hypothesis: when namespace resolver fell back to alias lookup it didn't validate the authenticated org claim against the resolved namespace owner. That allowed alias->namespace mapping to return org-a for tokens from org-b. KMS bindings still show keys bound to org-a (no decrypt logged yet).

rachel: Run an audit query and paste last 10 suspicious events. Also confirm no KMS decrypts crossed boundary. Suggest commands: 
```
# audit log query (internal)
SELECT timestamp, actor_org, actor_id, action, resource_org, resource_id
FROM audit_logs
WHERE action = 'projects.list' AND resource_org = 'org-a' AND actor_org <> 'org-a'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

maya: Pasted first results: 2026-03-20T12:07:21Z actor_org=org-b actor_id=user-872 action=projects.list resource_org=org-a resource_id=[proj-1, proj-2]
2026-03-20T12:08:03Z actor_org=org-b actor_id=user-333 action=projects.list resource_org=org-a resource_id=[proj-3]

oliver: Good catch. Immediate actions I propose:
- Revoke any short-lived tokens issued in the window 12:05-12:15 (auth service).
- Force namespace-resolver cache flush (CDN + local caches).
- Push hotfix to resolver to validate `actor.org == resolved_namespace.owner_org` before returning routing. PR #3430 queued.
- Confirm KMS audit: `kms.access` events for those users between 12:05-12:15.

rachel: Also: compliance notify (legal + CISO) if data exposure reaches project metadata with PII. File a report and mark timeline. I'll start the compliance ticket.

maya: I'm rotating any service tokens that might have been used by the resolver and kicking sessions for implicated users. Hotfix PR #3430 includes an explicit org-claim check and unit + integration tests.

oliver: Please add regression tests that assert alias fallback can't return a namespace owned by a different org than the authenticated claim. Add an audit event when alias fallback happens.

rachel: After hotfix we need a postmortem: timeline, root cause, why flag wasn't blocked, and why KMS checks didn't trip (or did they?). Also update the runbook to include `validate-namespace-owner` check and `revoke-window` script.

maya: Will update incident page with commands run and attach logs. Next update in 15m. :thumbsup:

oliver: I'll follow up with rollout rollback verification and ensure the feature flag stays disabled until we patch and run canary.

rachel: Thanks. Keep channel updated.
